title: A broad abstract meets one narrow experiment

statement.quote: Sprout improves classification accuracy across all image datasets and compute budgets.

assessment.reason: The supplied evidence covers MiniShapes at 10 epochs. It cannot establish improvement across all image datasets and compute budgets.

evidence.quote: The only accuracy experiment uses MiniShapes, the test split, and 10 training epochs.
No other dataset, compute budget, or distribution-shift evaluation is included in these materials.

assessment.limitations: No other dataset or training budget is supplied. This is a scope gap, not a demonstrated counterexample.
assessment.next_check: At a predeclared 1-epoch budget on MiniShapes, compare Sprout and Linear with the same split, tuning budget, metric, and seeds; report the paired per-seed differences.
assessment.falsifier: A controlled setting where Sprout has no positive mean accuracy difference would contradict the universal improvement claim.

statement.quote: On MiniShapes test data under the fixed 10-epoch protocol, Sprout reaches 82.0% accuracy.

assessment.reason: The qualified sentence matches the reported aggregate of 82.0% for the specified setting.

evidence.quote: Both models use three seeds (11, 22, 33); results.csv contains their unweighted mean accuracies on a 0-100 scale.
The accuracy protocol is fixed-v1. No confidence interval or significance test is supplied.

assessment.limitations: Only an aggregate is supplied. Neither individual seed scores nor statistical significance can be recovered.
assessment.next_check: Recompute the unweighted mean from the three original evaluation logs under fixed-v1.
assessment.falsifier: An independently recomputed mean outside 82.0 +/- 0.05 percentage points would conflict with the stated rounded value.

statement.quote: Under that protocol, Sprout exceeds Linear by 5.0 percentage points.

assessment.reason: The supplied aggregates imply a 2.0 percentage-point difference, which conflicts with the quoted 5.0.
assessment.limitations: This checks agreement with supplied aggregates; it does not establish which version of the paper or results is authoritative.
assessment.next_check: Reconcile the two aggregate values against the original evaluation logs and the manuscript version.
assessment.falsifier: If the authoritative values remain 82.0 and 80.0, the 5.0-point statement is contradicted.

statement.quote: Under identical hardware and batch settings, Sprout is 2.0 times faster than Linear.

assessment.reason: The arithmetic ratio is 2.0, but the timing rows use different hardware. The identical-hardware premise conflicts with the recorded settings.

evidence.quote: Sprout was timed on a GPU and Linear on a CPU, both at batch size 64 and FP32.

assessment.limitations: There is only one timing observation per model. Hardware is a confounder and variance is unavailable.
assessment.next_check: Time both models on the same device at batch 64 and FP32, using the same warmup, synchronization, and repeated-run protocol.
assessment.falsifier: A controlled baseline/method median time ratio below 2.0 would challenge the claimed twofold speed advantage.

statement.quote: Sprout remains accurate under distribution shift.

assessment.reason: No distribution-shift evaluation is supplied. The absence does not establish that Sprout fails under shift.

evidence.quote: No other dataset, compute budget, or distribution-shift evaluation is included in these materials.

assessment.limitations: The claim does not define the shift or what counts as remaining accurate.
assessment.next_check: Predeclare a concrete shift, such as a fixed blur corruption, and an accuracy-retention threshold; evaluate both clean and shifted MiniShapes test inputs.
assessment.falsifier: Retention below the predeclared threshold would challenge the operationalized robustness claim; no threshold or result is asserted here.

statement.quote: The in-distribution accuracy gain over Linear is 2.5% relative.

assessment.reason: The supplied accuracy aggregates imply a 2.5% relative increase over Linear in the described in-distribution setting.

evidence.quote: The only accuracy experiment uses MiniShapes, the test split, and 10 training epochs.

assessment.limitations: This relative arithmetic does not establish statistical significance or generalization.
assessment.next_check: Recompute both means from the original per-seed logs, preserving the same split and protocol.
assessment.falsifier: A recomputed relative increase outside 2.5 +/- 0.05 percent would conflict with the rounded claim.
